incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Increased 5xx rate on /api/generate from canary cohort. Triggered at 1897654321. Pager sent to #eng-oncall and #eng-infra. Link: https://monitoring.example/incidents/INC-2026-07-21-01
Alice Chen: oncall Alice here, ack. I'm looking at canary nodes now.
Alice Chen: grafana shows spike starting at 1897654280, error rate ~12% for canary only. Baseline is <0.5%.
deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-07-21T01:04Z -> service/api canary: image=registry.redwood/dev/api:latest (pushed by CI #5482)
Alice Chen: seeing pods in CrashLoopBackOff and a few 502s. Pull/digest looks odd, some pods show image digest A (sha256:aaaa1111) and others show digest B (sha256:bbbb2222) even though tag was identical.
Bob Patel: jumping in — we cut the canary using the mutable tag `latest` from CI. CI pushed an emergency rebuild last night; looks like the registry briefly pointed `latest` at a different digest while old canary controllers still referenced cached manifests -> possible tag mutation/cache mismatch.
Carlos Mendez: registry index reconciliation lag + CDN edge caching can cause a mix of manifests being served. That would explain mixed digests across nodes.
Dana Ortiz: customer impact? which routes affected?
Alice Chen: only canary route /api/generate/canary and ~3% of production traffic hit canaries. However some upstream routing was misconfigured so ~0.5% of prod requests spilled to canary subset -> those saw 5xx. Rough estimate: ~800 requests/min, ~40 customers experienced errors in last 15m.
Bob Patel: mitigation plan: 1) kill new canary flag to stop routing traffic to canary, 2) pin canary to known-good digest and force rollout, 3) purge mutable tag from registry and re-tag immutably, 4) CI fix to stop using mutable tags for canary.
Alice Chen: doing step 1 now — toggling feature flag to disable canary routing.
Alice Chen: /fd-toggle feature: disable_canary_routing = true -> response: ok
Alice Chen: traffic to canary dropped to 0% within 30s, error rate on prod endpoints back to baseline.
Dana Ortiz: executing pin + rollback recommendation. Which digest do we pin to?
Bob Patel: previous stable digest is sha256:cccc3333 (CI #5479). Use that.
Carlos Mendez: patching deployment to explicit image digest to avoid tag lookup. Run this:
```
kubectl set image deployment/api api=registry.redwood/prod/api@sha256:cccc3333 --namespace=prod --record
kubectl rollout status deployment/api --namespace=prod
```
Dana Ortiz: running the patch now.
Dana Ortiz: rollout in progress...
Dana Ortiz: rollout complete, all pods on sha256:cccc3333 and status Ready.
Alice Chen: monitoring -> 5xxs stopped, SLOs recovered.
registry-bot: Detected mutable tag usage: registry.redwood/dev/api:latest was updated 2x in the last 24h. Suggest making tags immutable and use digest pinning.
Bob Patel: I'll coordinate registry purge: remove `latest` from prod registry and create an immutable alias `ci-latest` only for ephemeral test clusters. Also updating CI to publish with `:ci-<buildnum>` and push an immutable tag (and never repurpose it).
Carlos Mendez: deployed short-term CDN manifest purge for registry endpoints to prevent stale cached manifests. Command used internally to CDN: `PURGE /v2/registry/.../manifests/latest` (internal tool).
Alice Chen: customer communication: no broad user-facing incident—impact limited to small subset. Operations: flagged as SEV3. Logging for affected requests captured; export saved to incident ticket INC-2026-07-21-01.
Bob Patel: root cause hypothesis: CI published a hotfix and reused the `latest` tag while older canaries still resolved to prior manifest via cache. Registry index reconciliation + CDN edge caching caused the mixed digests across nodes.
Alice Chen: actions/owner/timeline:
- Bob Patel: make tags immutable + CI changes (owner: Bob) — ETA 24h
- Carlos Mendez: CDN purge automation + registry cache metrics (owner: Carlos) — ETA 48h
- Dana Ortiz: post-incident verification and runbook update for canary rollouts (owner: Dana) — ETA 72h
- Alice Chen: write incident summary and add to #postmortems (owner: Alice) — ETA 24h
Alice Chen: handing off to Day team for follow-up (cc @Bob Patel @Carlos Mendez). Oncall clear for now.
Bob Patel: noted, will create follow-up tickets for CI and registry policy.
incident-bot: Incident resolved at 1897654499. Severity: SEV3. Mitigation: feature-flag kill-switch + pinned rollout + registry purge. Postmortem requested.
Alice Chen: thanks team. Adding timeline and logs to INC-2026-07-21-01 and scheduling a postmortem for tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
